job.title: Customer Service Team Leader

Public Sector People is partnering with a not-for-profit organisation to recruit a Team Leader - Customer Services on a six-month contract.

This is an opportunity for an experienced people leader who enjoys supporting a team, resolving complex enquiries and making practical improvements to how services are delivered.

About the opportunity

Reporting to the Projects and Operations Manager, you will oversee the day-to-day customer services function, ensuring people receive consistent, respectful and culturally appropriate support.

Leading a team of approximately seven, you will balance coaching and performance management with workflow coordination, escalated enquiries and service improvement. You will also review and approve eligible financial assistance requests and reimbursements within delegated authority.

Key responsibilities
  • Lead, coach and develop the team through regular feedback, one-to-one meetings and clear performance expectations.
  • Coordinate workloads, rostering, attendance and leave to maintain service capacity.
  • Act as an escalation point for complex, urgent or sensitive enquiries, supporting employees through challenging conversations.
  • Monitor service standards, KPIs and customer feedback, identifying issues and opportunities for improvement.
  • Review and approve eligible payments, reimbursements and support requests in accordance with policies and delegated authority.
  • Maintain accurate customer records and prepare reports on team performance, service demand and emerging trends.
  • Improve processes, systems and workflows in collaboration with other teams.
  • Support recruitment, onboarding and training, building a positive and accountable team culture.
About you

You will bring at least three years' experience leading and developing teams, ideally within customer service, contact centre or another high-volume service environment.

You will also demonstrate:
  • Proven experience coaching employees, managing performance and building team capability.
  • Experience coordinating workforce capacity, workloads, rostering or leave planning.
  • Strong communication skills and sound judgement when resolving complex or sensitive matters.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced and changing environment.
  • Confidence using CRM systems, reporting tools and operational data to monitor performance and guide improvements.
  • Strong organisation, attention to detail and a practical approach to problem-solving.
  • The ability to work within policies, procedures and approval frameworks.
  • Cultural sensitivity and a commitment to respectful, person-centred service.
Experience within not-for-profit, community services, charitable trusts or Aboriginal organisations would be valued, as would experience working respectfully with Aboriginal people, families and communities. Experience administering financial assistance, grants or reimbursements would also be beneficial.

Why apply?

This role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution over six months, supporting team development and improving the experience of people accessing services. It will suit someone who enjoys hands-on leadership and can bring structure, consistency and confidence to a busy customer services function.

Apply

job.title: Coordinator Revenue Services
job.description:
Coordinator Revenue Services
Livingstone Shire Council | Yeppoon, QLD | LGIA Level 6 | Starting at $109,779 + 13% super

Public Sector People are proud to partner with Livingstone Shire Council to recruit an experienced Coordinator Revenue Services.

This is an opportunity to step into a key leadership role within Council’s Financial Services team, overseeing the day-to-day operations of Revenue Services and leading a team of five.

Reporting to the Manager Financial Services, you will bring strong revenue and accounting expertise together with people leadership, stakeholder management and a continuous improvement mindset.

The role will play an important part in ensuring Council’s revenue operations are accurate, compliant and effective, while supporting the team through ongoing development, process improvement and knowledge sharing.

Relocation support is available for eligible candidates including up to $4,000 in relocation reimbursement and up to $2,000 in temporary accommodation support, subject to Council approval and conditions.

The Opportunity
As Coordinator Revenue Services, you will lead, develop and manage the Revenue team, ensuring high performance, operational effectiveness and a consistent approach to service delivery.

You will oversee Council’s revenue systems, rating structures and processes, while providing specialist advice across revenue, rates, fees and charges, debt recovery and related financial matters.

This is a hands-on leadership role where your ability to support and develop your team will be just as important as your technical revenue expertise.
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Leading, developing and managing the Revenue Services team to deliver high performance and continuous improvement
  • Overseeing revenue systems, rating structures and processes to ensure accurate billing, collection and legislative compliance
  • Providing expert revenue and financial advice to internal stakeholders and the community
  • Supporting the development and review of revenue policies, procedures and processes
  • Contributing to budgeting, financial reporting, strategic financial planning, audits, reconciliations and internal controls
  • Managing Council’s revenue accounts, fees and charges registers and associated processes
  • Identifying opportunities to improve revenue practices, systems and service delivery
  • Supporting effective resource management across the Revenue Services function
  • Building strong working relationships across Financial Services, Council and the broader community
  • Supporting the development of team capability, knowledge sharing and succession planning
  • Ensuring accurate records, sound governance and compliance with relevant legislation and Council policies
About You
You will be an experienced revenue or accounting professional who understands the complexities of revenue management and is confident leading a team in a local government or similar environment.

You’ll bring strong technical capability, but equally important will be your ability to lead people, build relationships and identify practical opportunities to improve the way revenue services are delivered.

You’ll bring:
  • Demonstrated experience in revenue accounting, rating legislation, debt recovery and/or related financial services
  • Strong understanding of rates, fees and charges and revenue processes
  • Proven people leadership and team management capability
  • Strong analytical, conceptual and problem-solving skills
  • The ability to interpret legislation, financial standards and Council policies and translate these into practical outcomes
  • Strong communication, consultation, negotiation and stakeholder management skills
  • Experience developing and improving policies, procedures and operational processes
  • Strong financial systems capability and sound organisational and time management skills
  • The ability to provide practical financial advice and work collaboratively across a range of stakeholders
  • A proactive approach to continuous improvement and team development
  • A strong commitment to professional and ethical conduct
You will also hold:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Business, Accounting or a related discipline
  • Substantial experience in a revenue management or accounting-focused position
  • Strong experience across financial and revenue management systems, with TechOne and Pathway experience highly regarded
  • A current C Class driver licence
Previous experience within a local government environment will be highly regarded, particularly experience across rates, revenue, recovery and property-related functions.

Why Livingstone Shire Council?
Livingstone Shire Council is located on Queensland’s Capricorn Coast, encompassing the communities of Yeppoon, Emu Park and surrounding rural areas.

This is an opportunity to join a regional Council and make a tangible contribution to the way revenue services are delivered to the local community.

The role offers:
  • Permanent, full-time employment
  • LGIA Level 6 classification
  • Relocation support of up to $4,000, plus up to $2,000 temporary accommodation support, for eligible relocations
  • Competitive starting salary of $109,779 + 13% superannuation
  • A nine-day fortnight supporting a strong work-life balance
  • The opportunity to lead a five-person Revenue Services team
  • A role with genuine scope to improve systems, processes and team capability
  • The opportunity to contribute to broader Financial Services outcomes
  • A supportive regional lifestyle on the Capricorn Coast
This is an opportunity for an experienced revenue professional to take on a leadership role where you can make a genuine impact, both through the technical work you deliver and the team you lead.

If you are an experienced revenue or accounting professional looking for a leadership opportunity within local government, we would like to hear from you.

job.description:

Job Requirements
  
Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, maintain and deliver integrated project plans and implementation activities.
  • Manage project schedules, risks, issues, dependencies, resources and critical path activities.
  • Coordinate integration activities across enterprise systems, business units, vendors and technical teams.

  • Prepare governance reports, presentations, decision papers and recommendations.
  • Manage vendor performance, contractual deliverables and procurement activities.

  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, influencing and negotiation capabilities.
  • Ability to work effectively across executive, operational and technical stakeholder groups.
  • Relevant qualifications in Information Technology, Project Management or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred Experience
  • Asset Management systems implementation or optimisation.

job.title: Automation Technician
job.description:
Industrial Automation Technologist / Technician

Location: Wetherill Park, Sydney
Industry: Advanced Manufacturing (Injection Moulding & Automation) Employment Type: Full-time, 24/7 manufacturing environment

About the Role
Our client, an established manufacturing operation based in Wetherill Park, is seeking an experienced Industrial Automation Technologist/Technician to join their team. This is a hands-on, technically diverse role supporting PLC-driven automation, industrial robotics, injection moulding machinery, and high-speed production equipment across a 24/7 site.

You'll be a key technical point of contact for production issues relating to equipment performance, product quality, and efficiency — working closely with Production, Maintenance, and Quality teams to minimise downtime and maximise OEE.
This role blends fault-finding, preventative maintenance, die setting, process optimisation, and continuous improvement, with genuine exposure to automation upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects.

Key Responsibilities
Automation & Technical Maintenance
  • Troubleshoot and maintain industrial automation and production equipment across a 24/7 environment
  • Service, repair, and set up injection moulding machines, industrial robots, IML systems, and auxiliary equipment
  • Fault-find and replace mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic components
  • Integrate industrial robots into material handling, inspection, and packaging applications, including safety interlock verification
  • Perform preventative and predictive maintenance, equipment upgrades, and calibrations
  • Complete major equipment overhauls and support complex machine, processing, and die-setting issues
Production & Process Support
  • Act as a key technical contact for production issues affecting output, quality, reliability, and efficiency
  • Perform die, insert, and colour changes, including machine start-ups and shutdowns
  • Set, adjust, and optimise robotics, machine software, and production process parameters
  • Troubleshoot production faults, including IML and high-speed packaging equipment
  • Maintain target cycle times while ensuring finished products meet specification
Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving
  • Investigate recurring and new faults using structured root-cause analysis; implement corrective and preventative actions
  • Analyse downtime, rejects, defects, and waste to identify improvement opportunities
  • Support automation design, programming, commissioning, and equipment upgrades
  • Maintain accurate records of downtime, rejects, NCRs, maintenance activities, and corrective actions
Quality & Compliance
  • Work closely with Quality Assurance to ensure equipment and processes meet product, customer, and regulatory requirements
  • Ensure compliance with site quality systems, HACCP, and applicable food safety requirements
  • Verify new or modified automation systems before production handover
Safety & Team Support
  • Work in line with WHS legislation, site safety procedures, and permit requirements
  • Identify, report, and rectify hazards and near misses
  • Coordinate with third-party service technicians when required
  • Support training and technical upskilling of production and maintenance personnel
  • Communicate and escalate technical issues across shifts to maintain operational continuity
About You
  • Proven experience in industrial automation, robotics, and/or injection moulding within a manufacturing environment
  • Strong mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic fault-finding skills
  • Experience with PLC-driven systems and industrial robot integration
  • Die-setting experience highly regarded
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, 24/7 production environment
  • Strong root-cause analysis and continuous improvement mindset
  • Food safety/HACCP exposure an advantage
  • Ability to train and support colleagues, and communicate effectively across shifts
Why Apply
  • Stable, full-time opportunity with genuine exposure to modern automation technology
  • Hands-on role combining automation, robotics, and process engineering — not a narrow, single-skill position
  • Real input into equipment upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects
  • Work within an established, well-resourced manufacturing operation

job.description:
Design & Build are partnering with a leading Australian residential building organisation to recruit a BIM / Archicad Trainer to join their People Development function.

Based in the Hunter Region, this role will support drafting teams nationally and will involve regular travel, both interstate and nationally.

Importantly, you don't need to already be an experienced trainer.

We're equally interested in hearing from experienced Archicad 29 users, Senior Drafters, BIM specialists or technical drafting professionals who enjoy helping others and would like to pivot their career into training and development.

For the right technical person, the business is prepared to invest in your development and support you in completing your Certificate IV in Training & Assessment.

The Role
Working closely with the BIM Manager and Learning & Development team, you'll become a key technical resource supporting drafting teams across the organisation.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Delivering Archicad and BIM training to drafting teams across Australia
  • Supporting the onboarding and technical induction of new starters
  • Developing structured Archicad training programs
  • Creating training materials including guides, videos, e-learning content, job aids and SOPs
  • Running face-to-face and virtual training sessions
  • Working one-on-one and with small groups to improve technical capability
  • Identifying knowledge gaps and opportunities to improve BIM processes and training
  • Working with internal technical specialists and external BIM providers
  • Monitoring training participation and effectiveness
  • Travelling nationally to support teams across different locations
About You
There are two backgrounds we're particularly interested in:

Experienced Trainer: You may already be delivering BIM, Archicad, CAD or technical training and be looking for an opportunity within a large national organisation.

Experienced Archicad User Ready for a Career Pivot: You may be a Senior Drafter, BIM Coordinator, Archicad specialist or highly experienced residential drafting professional who loves helping others and wants to move away from day-to-day drafting into a training-focused career.
Ideally, you'll bring:
  • Strong Archicad experience – Archicad 29 highly regarded
  • A background in drafting, BIM or residential construction
  • Confidence communicating technical information in a simple way
  • Strong interpersonal and presentation skills
  • An interest in coaching, mentoring and developing others
  • The ability and willingness to travel nationally
  • A proactive approach to technology and continuous improvement
  • A current driver's licence
A Certificate IV in Training & Assessment is advantageous but not essential – support can be provided to obtain this qualification for the right candidate.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is a unique opportunity to take your technical Archicad knowledge and turn it into a long-term career in training and capability development.
You'll join a major Australian building organisation, work closely with BIM and L&D specialists, gain exposure to drafting teams nationally and have the opportunity to become a recognised technical training specialist within the business.
If you're an Archicad expert who's always the person others come to for help, this could be the career pivot you've been looking for.

Apply now or contact Renee Hamilton at Design & Build Recruitment for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Information Access Manager
job.description:
Location: Sydney, NSW
Salary: $178,021 to $203,376 + 12% Super
Work Type: Full Time, Permanent
Public Sector People on behalf of City of Sydney

Lead the City's information access function and become the trusted expert driving transparency, sound decision making and best practice governance across one of Australia's most progressive councils.

Public Sector People are proud to partner with the City of Sydney to recruit an Information Access Manager within the Digital and Information Services Unit.

This is a unique opportunity for an experienced GIPA or Freedom of Information professional to lead the City's information access function as its delegated decision-maker under the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009. Leading a specialist team, you'll make complex statutory decisions, provide trusted advice to the Executive Leadership Team and work across every area of the organisation to ensure the City continues to uphold the principles of transparency, accountability and open government.

This is a role for someone who enjoys applying legislation to complex situations, can confidently make independent decisions and has the judgement to navigate sensitive matters with professionalism, diplomacy and integrity.

About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Information Services, you will be responsible for:
  • Lead and develop the City's specialist Information Access team.
  • Act as the City's delegated decision-maker under the GIPA Act.
  • Assess and determine complex GIPA applications, subpoenas and other information access matters.
  • Provide expert advice to Directors, Executives and business units on information access legislation and disclosure obligations.
  • Represent the City in reviews with the Information and Privacy Commission and NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT).
  • Drive proactive release initiatives and promote a culture of open government across the organisation.
  • Develop policies, procedures and education programs that strengthen legislative compliance and organisational capability.
  • Work collaboratively with Legal, Governance, Archives and operational teams to resolve complex information access matters.
 
 
What You'll Bring
  • Extensive experience administering the Government Information (Public Access) Act (GIPA) or equivalent Freedom of Information legislation.
  • Demonstrated experience making independent statutory decisions within a complex public sector environment.
  • Strong understanding of balancing transparency with public interest considerations and legislative obligations.
  • Experience advising senior executives and confidently influencing stakeholders on sensitive matters.
  • Leadership experience managing and developing high-performing specialist teams.
  • Excellent judgement, resilience and communication skills, with the confidence to make, explain and defend complex decisions.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Information Management, Governance or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.


Why City of Sydney?
  • Lead the City's information access function as the delegated decision-maker under the GIPA Act.
  • Make decisions that directly influence transparency, governance and public trust.
  • Work closely with senior executives, Legal and Governance on complex and high-profile matters.
  • Join one of Australia's leading local government organisations, committed to innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement.
  
Ready to become the trusted authority on information access at the City of Sydney?

Contact Esme Lynch at Public Sector People on 0413 282 765 or email esme@publicsectorpeople.com.au for a confidential discussion.

Applications close: 11:59pm, Thursday 15th October 2026.

job.description:
Tenancy Manager 

Our client is a well-established community housing provider delivering safe, affordable and sustainable homes across New South Wales. Their work goes beyond housing - partnering with tenants, community groups, and support services to strengthen wellbeing and build thriving communities.

They are seeking a values-driven Tenancy Manager to join their customer-focused team and play a key role in delivering exceptional tenancy management and community outcomes.

The Opportunity

In this hands-on role, you’ll be the first point of contact for tenants, ensuring their needs are met with care, professionalism and responsiveness. You’ll manage a diverse tenancy portfolio, supporting residents to sustain their housing through proactive engagement and practical problem-solving.

You’ll also work collaboratively with internal teams and external partners to address tenancy issues, manage arrears and property care, and contribute to broader community wellbeing initiatives.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide responsive, respectful and consistent customer service
  • Manage tenancy agreements in line with the NSW Residential Tenancies Act 2010
  • Support tenants to sustain their tenancies through early intervention and engagement
  • Manage arrears, property standards, and anti-social behaviour
  • Prepare documentation and represent the organisation at NCAT where required
  • Collaborate with colleagues and support partners to achieve positive tenant outcomes
  • Maintain accurate records and comply with organisational policies and reporting standards
About You

You’re an organised and empathetic professional who thrives in a busy, people-focused environment. You bring a mix of practical tenancy management skills and a genuine commitment to community impact.

Essential:
  • Experience in property management (community housing, public housing, or real estate)
  • Sound understanding of the NSW Residential Tenancies Act 2010
  • Strong communication, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills
  • Self-motivated, with the ability to work autonomously and as part of a team
  • Current NSW Driver’s Licence
Desirable:
  • Understanding of social and affordable housing frameworks
  • Experience engaging with vulnerable communities
  • Prior NCAT representation experience
  • Qualifications in social work, community services or a related discipline
What’s on Offer
  • Hybrid working model (4 days onsite / 1 day WFH)
  • Supportive, values-led culture focused on inclusion and empowerment
  • Opportunity to make a tangible difference in people’s lives and communities
If you’re a housing professional who combines a business head with a social heart, this role offers a meaningful opportunity to make a lasting impact.

Apply now or contact Public Sector People for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Project Manager (Housing)
job.description:
Project Manager (Housing)
 
A new building is only part of the picture. Making it ready for people to call home takes coordinated planning, clear decisions and strong operational leadership.
 
Public Sector People is seeking a Project Manager for a purpose-led organisation delivering social and affordable housing across Greater Brisbane and surrounding areas.
 
This role will bring new housing developments, acquisitions and service expansions into operation, ensuring properties, teams, systems and services are ready before residents move in.
 
Based in Brisbane, with travel to development and property sites, you will lead a team of two and work across the organisation to coordinate delivery, resolve challenges and oversee the transition into stable day-to-day operations.
 
The opportunity
 
You will take ownership of the operational readiness program, translating development commitments into practical plans with clear milestones, responsibilities and measures of success.
 
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading readiness plans across multiple projects, managing timelines, budgets, resources, risks and dependencies.
  • Coordinating property handovers, including asset information, defects, compliance documentation, utilities and contractor mobilisation.
  • Bringing together tenant allocations, sign-ups, move-ins and customer communications to support a coordinated occupancy process.
  • Ensuring systems, data, procedures, staffing and training are prepared and tested before opening.
  • Leading cross-functional working groups and working with developers, builders, government agencies, contractors and service partners.
  • Providing executive reporting and recommendations on readiness, emerging risks and decisions required.
  • Supporting early operations and transferring outstanding actions and ongoing responsibilities to the relevant teams.
About you
 
You will bring substantial experience delivering complex projects, operational mobilisation, service transitions or major change initiatives involving multiple teams and stakeholders.
 
You can turn competing requirements into a clear delivery plan, build commitment across business functions and make sound decisions when priorities shift.
 
You will also bring:
  • Strong project governance skills, including integrated planning, risk management, assurance and executive reporting.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing stakeholders across an organisation.
  • Financial and commercial capability, including budget management, forecasting, procurement and supplier coordination.
  • Clear communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
  • Practical knowledge of WHS, privacy, records management and operational compliance.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification or an equivalent combination of expertise and senior project experience.
  • A current Queensland driver licence and willingness to complete a National Police Check.
Experience in community housing, human services, property development, construction handover or asset management would be valuable. Experience opening new residential properties or services, implementing systems or managing data migration would also be well regarded.
 
What's on offer
  • Full-time hours, 38 hours per week.
  • A broad leadership role with autonomy and visibility across the organisation.
  • The opportunity to shape how new housing and services are brought into operation.
  • Work that contributes to safe, secure and affordable homes.
To apply
 
Apply with your resume outlining your relevant project delivery and operational mobilisation experience.

Public Sector People are partnering with a large State government Department in BRISBANE to recruit an experienced Technical Business Analyst for an initial 6-month temp contract position + potential extension.

This hands-on role requires an experienced analyst who can thrive in a fast-paced environment, bring clarity to ambiguity and deliver practical outcomes.

  • Document data requirements, business rules, data definitions, data quality standards and migration needs for legacy and external data sources.
  • Identify and resolve requirement gaps, conflicts, dependencies and risks, ensuring requirements remain traceable throughout design, testing and implementation.
  • Facilitate workshops with business, technical and vendor stakeholders to gather requirements, solve issues and support delivery, testing and operational readiness.
  

The ideal candidate will have:
  • Strong Technical Business Analyst experience delivering complex technology projects involving multiple systems, data flows and business processes.
  • Proven ability to gather, define and document business, functional, data and integration requirements, including data mapping and validation.
  • Experience working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, driving analysis activities and achieving stakeholder alignment across business, technical and vendor teams.
  
Highly Desirable attributes:
  • Experience in regulated or operational environments such as government, transport, compliance, enforcement or safety-critical industries.
  • Background working with asset management or enterprise asset management platforms, ideally Hardcat or similar COTS solutions.
  • Experience with APIs, system integrations, data synchronisation and integration monitoring.
  • Strong data migration experience involving complex legacy system transitions.
  • Experience working with software vendors, implementation partners and managed service providers.

  • Lead the project through to completion, defects and final handover
About You
We are looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager who has a proven track record delivering large-scale multi-residential, student accommodation, build-to-rent, hotel or similarly complex commercial projects.

Ideally, you will have:
  • 10+ years' construction experience, with significant PM experience

  • Strong multi-residential or high-density residential experience
  • Student accommodation, build-to-rent, hotel or large-scale apartment experience highly regarded

You will be joining an established Tier 2 / major commercial construction business with a strong reputation for delivering complex projects across Melbourne.
The business has an established pipeline across multi-residential, student accommodation, commercial and other large-scale developments, with a focus on quality delivery and long-term client relationships.
This is not a business where you will simply be another number on a major project. The successful candidate will have genuine responsibility for delivery and will work closely with senior leadership.

Why Join?

job.title: Coordinator Open Spaces Strategy
job.description:
Clarence Valley Council is seeking an experienced and versatile leader to coordinate the strategic planning, asset management and capital delivery of its extensive open-space network.
  
Covering an area of more than 10,000 square kilometres and incorporating communities including Grafton, Maclean and Yamba, the Clarence Valley offers the opportunity to work across a varied portfolio of parks, reserves, sporting facilities, beaches, aquatic facilities and public recreation infrastructure.
  
The Role
Reporting to the Manager Open Spaces and Facilities, you will lead Council’s Open Spaces Strategy team and coordinate the long-term planning and improvement of the open-space network.
  
This is a broad, strategic position rather than an operational parks role. You will connect planning, asset management and project delivery to ensure Council makes informed, sustainable decisions about its public spaces and facilities.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading the development and review of open-space strategies, policies, masterplans and providing advice to inform the development of plans of management
  • Improving asset management plans, service levels and lifecycle planning across the open-space portfolio
  • Coordinating the planning, procurement and delivery of capital works projects
  • Managing service contracts and licence agreements relating to aquatic, sporting and beach facilities
  • Providing professional advice on development applications and projects affecting public open space, landscaping, vegetation and trees
  • Responding to emerging asset issues and balancing reactive requests with longer-term priorities
  • Preparing Council reports, funding applications, project documentation and evidence-based recommendations
  • Leading a multidisciplinary team and working closely with operational staff, contractors, community groups and internal stakeholders
About You
You will be an established leader who can operate across several disciplines rather than working within one narrow area of expertise.

You may come from open-space planning, asset management, engineering, landscape architecture, recreation planning, urban and regional planning or capital project delivery. More important than a particular professional background is your ability to connect strategic planning with practical implementation.

You will bring:
  • Experience developing strategies, policies, masterplans or asset management plans
  • Practical experience delivering capital works or construction-related projects
  • Sound project, contract and budget management capability
  • Established leadership experience and the ability to provide clear direction to a multidisciplinary team
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
  • The judgement to manage competing priorities and politically or publicly sensitive matters
  • The ability to interpret asset data, technical information, planning requirements and Council policies
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or an equivalent combination of qualifications and experience
Local government experience will be highly regarded, particularly where you have worked across community-facing services and managed changing operational and political priorities.

The Opportunity
This position offers a rare opportunity to influence the future of a diverse and highly visible community asset portfolio. You will have the scope to strengthen Council’s strategic and asset management approach while delivering projects that directly shape how residents and visitors experience the Clarence Valley.
  
Council offers:
  • A permanent full-time position
  • Salary of $108,853–$129,809 plus superannuation
  • 70 hours per fortnight
  • Flexible working hours and access to flex time
  • Five days of MyLeave each year, which can be used flexibly for any purpose
  • Professional development and career progression opportunities
  • The lifestyle benefits of living and working in the NSW Northern Rivers

The role has been created to support continued growth, strengthen the capability of the project management team and maintain strong delivery performance as the business scales.

You will lead and develop the Victorian Project Management team while continuing to personally deliver larger and more complex projects.
Approximately 50% of the role will be focused on project delivery and 50% on leading, mentoring and developing the PM team.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead and develop the Victorian Project Management team
  • Oversee a project portfolio in VIC of approximately $40M per annum
  • Personally manage a number of larger and more complex projects, generally up to $6M
  • Provide leadership, coaching and mentoring to Project Managers and developing talent
  • Maintain strong relationships with subcontractors, consultants, clients, landlords, building managers and authorities
  • Take responsibility for project profitability, commercial performance and risk
  • Negotiate and manage head contracts, variations and commercial outcomes
  • Develop and manage project programmes and ensure delivery against key milestones
  • Maintain oversight of cost planning, procurement, contract administration and project controls
  • Identify and manage commercial and delivery risks across the portfolio
  • Continue to build and leverage an established Victorian subcontractor and consultant network
  • Contribute to the broader national delivery leadership group and strategic direction of the business
  • Help develop processes, standards and capability as the Victorian operation continues to grow
About You

We are looking for an experienced commercial fitout professional who has progressed through project delivery and wants to take the next step into senior leadership, without stepping away from projects.

You will ideally have:
  • Significant experience delivering commercial fitout, interiors or construction projects
  • Experience managing projects above $5M+
  • Strong commercial understanding across cost, programme, contracts, variations and risk
  • Experience negotiating and administering head contracts
  • A strong understanding of project profitability and P&L responsibility
  • The ability to develop and manage your own project programmes
  • Strong relationships across the Victorian subcontractor and consultant market
  • Experience working with clients, consultants, QSs, superintendents, landlords and other project stakeholders
  • Leadership or mentoring experience, with the ability to develop high-performing PMs
  • A hands-on approach to project delivery and a genuine interest in remaining close to the work
  • A relevant qualification in Construction Management, Project Management, Building or a related discipline
Leadership experience is important, but you do not necessarily need to have already hold a Director title. The opportunity could suit an established senior PM ready to step into leadership, as well as an existing construction leader looking for greater responsibility.

Why This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to join a business where project delivery and commercial performance are directly connected to the business, rather than operating within the margins and structures of a much larger builder.
You will have genuine influence over the Victorian operation, while remaining actively involved in project delivery.

The role offers a clear pathway for someone who wants to progress into senior leadership while retaining the technical and commercial side of construction that they enjoy.

If you think this role sounds like the suitable next step for your career, please contact Sophia from Design and Build Recruitment or click 'Apply'.

job.title: Civil Works Manager
job.description:
Civil Works Manager

North Burnett Regional Council | Mundubbera, QLD | Civil Works & Infrastructure | Base salary up to $200K + housing support + vehicle allowance
  
North Burnett Regional Council is seeking a Civil Works Manager to lead its civil works and open spaces functions across the region. With a base salary of up to $200,000, this is an opportunity for an experienced infrastructure leader to shape service delivery, develop people and make a visible difference across six townships.
  
This position suits a pro-active leader who will get out across the region, spend time with their teams, understand the condition of the network, visit works in progress and actively resolve the issues that impact employees and the community.
  
With teams operating across six townships, visibility matters. The successful candidate will be expected to build strong relationships with staff, provide clear direction and create an environment where people feel supported, developed and accountable.
  
The Role
  
Reporting to the General Manager Works, you will lead the delivery of Council's civil works services across a diverse regional portfolio encompassing rural and urban roads, bridges, parks and open spaces, aerodromes and cemeteries.
The immediate priorities include strengthening delivery across the road network and supporting the people who deliver it.
  
Council is rebuilding momentum across its civil works program, with a strong focus on road renewals, resheeting, resealing and bridge repairs. You'll inherit capable people within the team, while having the opportunity to strengthen leadership, develop emerging talent and improve how works are planned, prioritised and delivered.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  
  • Providing visible, hands-on leadership across geographically dispersed civil works and open spaces teams
  • Leading, coaching and developing staff while building accountability, capability and succession
  • Overseeing the delivery and maintenance of Council's rural and urban road networks and associated infrastructure
  • Developing maintenance programs and identifying renewal priorities through sound asset management practices
  • Leading the planning and delivery of Council's civil capital works program
  • Managing operational and capital budgets and ensuring resources are directed to the areas of greatest need
  • Driving improvements in productivity, plant utilisation, safety and service delivery
  • Working closely with contractors, consultants and internal teams to achieve value-for-money outcomes
  • Building trusted relationships with stakeholders and communities across the North Burnett region
  • Providing clear, consistent and evidence-based advice while following issues through to resolution.
  
The formal position description reinforces this emphasis on visible leadership, staff capability, accountability and safety alongside asset management and capital delivery.
  
About You
  
You are an experienced civil works or infrastructure professional, but importantly, you are a leader who enjoys being involved.
  
You'll be comfortable walking into a depot and talking with frontline employees, visiting a road or project to understand an issue firsthand, mentoring an engineer who wants to progress their career, and then presenting clear and credible advice to senior leadership or elected members.
  
You will bring:
  • Strong experience across civil works, roads, infrastructure maintenance or construction
  • Proven experience leading operational and geographically dispersed teams
  • A hands-on and highly visible leadership style
  • A genuine commitment to coaching, mentoring and developing people
  • Strong asset management and capital works planning capability
  • Sound commercial, financial and project management experience
  • A practical understanding of safety within civil construction and maintenance environments
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to engage equally well with frontline staff, technical professionals, executives and elected members
  • Energy, initiative and a willingness to challenge existing ways of working and implement improvements
  • High levels of integrity, accountability and follow-through.
  
Council is open-minded regarding where you have developed your experience. You may already be working within local or state government, or you may come from civil construction, consulting or another infrastructure environment and be looking to bring your experience into a broader community-focused leadership role. The client specifically confirmed that local government experience is not essential and is interested in candidates who bring energy, ideas and the ability to implement change.
  
A Civil Engineering background and RPEQ would be highly regarded although this is not essential. More important is having the technical credibility to be an informed client and provide sound leadership across the function.
  
Why Join North Burnett Regional Council?
  
This is a role where you can see the impact of your leadership.
  
You'll have the opportunity to strengthen an established team, develop future leaders, rebuild momentum across the road network and introduce new ideas that improve how Council delivers services to its communities. Council sees a genuine opportunity for innovation and more cost-effective delivery as it continues a multi-year program of rebuilding its road network.
  
The package includes:
  • Base salary up to $200,000, depending on experience
  • $25,000 vehicle allowance
  • Remote locality allowance
  • $5,000 professional development allowance
  • Five weeks annual leave plus leave loading
  • Relocation assistance for the successful candidate
  • Access to Council housing in Mundubbera
  
If you're a civil infrastructure professional who believes leadership means being present, developing your people, communicating clearly and taking ownership of outcomes, this is an opportunity to have a genuine impact across an entire region.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the 'Apply Now' button or contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People
E: adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close Friday 9th October at 5pm

job.title: Municipal Building Surveyor | Hobsons Bay City Council
job.description:
About Hobsons Bay City Council

Hobsons Bay City Council serves a diverse and established municipality in Melbourne’s inner west, encompassing residential neighbourhoods, established activity centres, industrial precincts and a range of community and Council assets.

Council’s building services function plays an important role in protecting community safety, responding to illegal building work and ensuring statutory obligations under the Building Act and Regulations are effectively delivered.

The service has recently undergone a realignment that has introduced clearer leadership across its two operational streams. A Deputy Municipal Building Surveyor now leads the building surveying function, while a Senior Building Surveyor oversees building site compliance and associated local laws activity.
This provides the incoming Municipal Building Surveyor with an experienced and stable team, a capable leadership structure and a strong platform from which to consolidate recent improvements and guide the future direction of the service.

Hobsons Bay is a values-led organisation committed to providing practical, responsive and community-focused services.

About the Role

The Municipal Building Surveyor is responsible for administering Council’s statutory building functions and providing leadership, technical oversight and strategic direction to an established team of approximately 11 staff.

The team operates across two complementary streams. The building surveying function includes the Deputy Municipal Building Surveyor, building surveyors, inspection, technical and administrative support. The building site compliance function is led by a Senior Building Surveyor and includes officers responsible for site safety and relevant local laws provisions.

The service undertakes a relatively small volume of municipal building permit work, with its primary focus sitting across enforcement, illegal building work, building safety and Council’s broader statutory responsibilities.

The incoming MBS will be supported by experienced practitioners who understand the municipality and service well. The team has good continuity, including several long-standing employees, and the recently appointed Deputy MBS provides capable day-to-day leadership across the building surveying function.

A recent review of the service identified a range of opportunities to strengthen processes, systems and operational practices. Many of these actions have already been progressed, with the new MBS responsible for ensuring improvements are fully embedded and that the service remains organised, responsive and transparent in reporting its workload, risks and priorities.
The role will also provide advice on emerging compliance matters, including swimming pool and spa safety obligations, while considering how Council can best support affected property owners and the wider community.

Over time, there is also scope to explore the future service model, including whether Council should broaden elements of its permit or inspection offering. Any future direction will need to be carefully considered against statutory responsibilities, organisational risk, insurance requirements and community benefit.

About You

You are an experienced building surveyor with Unlimited registration in Victoria and the technical capability required to perform the statutory responsibilities of a Municipal Building Surveyor.

You bring strong knowledge of building legislation, enforcement, compliance and regulatory decision-making, ideally developed across local government, private building surveying or a combination of both environments.
You are a practical and engaged leader who can provide clear technical direction while empowering an established Deputy MBS and senior practitioners to manage their respective areas effectively.

This is not a role requiring wholesale change. You will take the time to understand what is working, establish visibility over the team’s workload and priorities, and ensure recent improvements to systems and processes are sustained.

You are comfortable making considered statutory decisions, managing complex or sensitive enforcement matters and providing clear advice to senior leaders. You also bring the curiosity and commercial awareness to consider how the service could evolve while maintaining an appropriate focus on risk, community safety and Council’s legislative obligations.
Most importantly, you will bring energy, sound judgement and a collaborative leadership style to a team with strong technical knowledge and a genuine commitment to the Hobsons Bay community.

Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Hobsons Bay City Council to recruit this important statutory leadership position.

For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Marcel Lafontaine at Public Sector People.

To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link. Applications close at October 15th at 5PM

job.title: Contract Administrator - Commercial

The Opportunity
We are currently representing a well-established and growing Tier 3 commercial construction business in Melbourne that is looking to add a Contract Administrator to their team.

The business has traditionally delivered projects in the $1M–$15M range and is now targeting projects up to approximately $30M, creating opportunities for ambitious CAs to work on larger projects and progress their careers alongside the growth of the company.

About the Builder
The business has been operating for over a decade and has built a strong reputation for delivering quality projects across a diverse range of sectors, including:
  • Education & tertiary
  • Healthcare & health
  • Pharmaceutical
  • Commercial
  • Childcare & aged care
  • Community
  • Sports & recreation

They work with a combination of government departments, universities, councils, institutional clients and private-sector clients, giving the team exposure to a broad range of construction environments.

The Role
As a Contract Administrator, you will work closely with the Project Manager and broader project team across the commercial and contractual delivery of projects.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing subcontractor procurement and letting packages
  • Preparing scopes of works and subcontract documentation
  • Reviewing and assessing subcontractor claims
  • Processing progress claims and variations
  • Managing variations, EOTs and contractual correspondence
  • Cost tracking and forecasting
  • Maintaining project budgets and financial reporting
  • Subcontractor negotiation and relationship management
  • Reviewing contracts and commercial risk
  • Assisting with project programming and procurement
  • Working closely with the PM and site team to ensure commercial and construction requirements are aligned
  • Maintaining accurate project documentation and reporting
  • Supporting the project from procurement through to completion and final account
Project Exposure
The business delivers projects across a variety of sectors, with previous and current work including university facilities, education projects, community infrastructure, childcare, health and commercial developments.
The company is also expanding into larger $5M–$30M projects, meaning there is scope for the successful candidate to gain exposure to progressively larger and more complex builds.
There is also an expanding pipeline of pharmaceutical projects, including work outside Victoria, providing further opportunities as the business grows.

What They're Looking For
We're interested in speaking with CAs who have:
  • 3+ years' experience in a commercial construction environment
  • Experience working for a Tier 2, Tier 3 or reputable commercial builder
  • Strong subcontractor management and procurement experience
  • Good understanding of contracts, variations, claims and EOTs
  • Strong attention to detail and commercial awareness
  • Good communication and negotiation skills
  • The ability to work closely with both PMs and Site Managers
  • A genuine interest in progressing their construction career
A construction-related qualification is preferred, although relevant practical experience will also be considered.

Why Consider It? This isn't simply another CA position.
The business is actively growing its project size and capability, meaning the successful candidate will have the opportunity to develop alongside the company rather than stepping into a role with a fixed ceiling.
You'll be joining a relatively lean team where CAs have genuine exposure to senior management, clients, subcontractors and project delivery, rather than being one of many people within a large corporate structure.
The leadership team is particularly focused on retaining good people long term, developing their staff and creating clear opportunities for progression.
The Ideal Candidate This role would suit a CA who has built a solid foundation in commercial construction and is now looking for:
More responsibility.
Larger projects.
Greater exposure to senior management.
And a genuine long-term pathway within a growing builder.

If you're a CA who wants to be part of a business where your contribution is visible and there is room to grow, I'd be keen to have a confidential conversation.
Apply now or contact Kristina for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Strategic Planner - Strategic Land Use
job.description:
The Council are looking for a motivated and skilled planner who can contribute to shaping the future of the community through strategic planning initiatives, policy implementation, and collaboration across Council and with external stakeholders.
  
Working within the Planning and Environment team, this role will contribute to the implementation and review of planning schemes, strategic projects, and land use strategies that support sustainable regional development.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  • Deliver high-quality strategic planning services, including reports, assessments, and professional advice to support Council planning processes and decision-making.
  • Assist with the implementation, maintenance, and amendment of planning schemes, strategic planning instruments, and infrastructure charging frameworks.
  • Interpret and apply relevant legislation, policies, and guidelines, including the Planning Act 2016 and Minister’s Guidelines and Rules.
  • Develop and contribute to strategic land use planning projects, including strategies, master plans, precinct plans, and placemaking initiatives.
  • Prepare clear and professional reports, correspondence, and planning advice for internal stakeholders, external clients, and the community.
  • Work collaboratively across Council to share knowledge, improve processes, and support organizational outcomes.

  • Maintain compliance with Work Health and Safety requirements, taking reasonable care for the health and safety of yourself and others.
  
The Successful Candidate
The successful candidate will be an experienced strategic planner with a strong understanding of legislative frameworks and a passion for shaping sustainable communities.
  • A solid understanding of the Planning Act 2016, Minister’s Guidelines and Rules, and other relevant planning legislation and policies.
  • At least three years’ experience in a town planning or strategic planning role, particularly involving the development of strategic planning instruments.
  • Experience in strategic land use planning, including the preparation of strategies, master plans, precinct plans, or placemaking projects.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce high-quality reports and advice.
  • Proven ability to build relationships and negotiate positive outcomes with a range of stakeholders, including in politically sensitive environments.
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills, with strong attention to detail.
  • A degree in Urban and Regional Planning or a related discipline from a recognized university.
  • A Queensland C Class driver’s license (minimum provisional).
  
  
Desirable experience includes:
  • Experience working in local or state government planning environments.
  • Involvement in drafting or amending planning schemes and strategic planning documents.
  • Experience with community engagement processes.
  • Knowledge of heritage or conservation planning, including historic buildings or culturally significant sites.
  • Eligibility for membership of a relevant professional planning association.

job.title: Planning Coordinator
job.description:
About Strathbogie Shire Council

Strathbogie Shire Council is a progressive regional municipality encompassing communities including Euroa, Nagambie, Avenel and Violet Town, ideally positioned between Melbourne and Shepparton.

Council is committed to delivering responsive, consistent and customer-focused planning services while supporting the sustainable growth and development of the Shire.

With a capable team in place and several significant planning matters progressing across the municipality, this is an opportunity to provide experienced leadership, strengthen internal capability and help shape the continued development of Council’s planning function.

About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Planning and Investment, the Planning Coordinator will lead Council’s statutory planning function while contributing to strategic planning projects, planning scheme amendments and broader service improvement initiatives.

This is a hands-on leadership position. You will provide clear direction and technical guidance to a developing team while personally managing complex and sensitive planning applications, including major subdivisions and proposals attracting significant community or Councillor interest.

You will oversee workloads, priorities and service standards, review technical assessments and reports, and support planners to develop their judgement, confidence and understanding of the Victorian planning system.

The role will work closely with applicants, internal stakeholders, referral authorities, community members and Councillors. You will prepare and present reports directly to Council, brief Councillors on significant planning matters and represent Council at VCAT, panel hearings and other planning forums when required.

While the role is weighted toward statutory planning, exposure to strategic planning will be highly regarded. You will also support policy development, planning scheme amendments and longer-term growth initiatives, enabling the Manager to focus more broadly across the performance and strategic direction of the unit.

About You

You are an experienced statutory and strategic planning professional ready to take genuine ownership of a small and important planning function.
You bring strong technical knowledge of the Planning and Environment Act, the Victorian Planning Provisions and contemporary local government planning practice. You are confident assessing complex applications, preparing defensible recommendations and navigating matters involving competing stakeholder, community and political interests.

Just as importantly, you are a capable people leader. You can set expectations, manage performance and workloads, develop emerging planners and create a culture of accountability, collaboration and support. You enjoy sharing your knowledge but also understand that leadership is about enabling others to perform rather than simply providing technical answers.

You are comfortable operating with autonomy and do not require significant day-to-day direction. You can identify issues early, exercise sound professional judgement and provide your Manager with the confidence that the statutory planning function is being effectively led.

Customer service is central to your approach. You communicate clearly, manage difficult conversations constructively and understand the importance of helping applicants and community members.

Most importantly, you are motivated by the opportunity to lead, support a developing team and build a high-performing planning service within a growing regional municipality.

Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Strathbogie Shire Council to recruit this important leadership opportunity.

For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the Position Description, please contact Marcel Lafontaine at Public Sector People -
marcel@publicsectorpeople.com.au.

To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.
Applications close - Wednesday October 14th 2026

Your responsibilities will include:

Energy & Resources recruitment experience would be highly regarded, but it is not essential.

More important is a strong understanding of the WA market, a proven ability to build lasting client relationships and established credibility within a specialist recruitment sector.

We are open to leaders from Energy, Resources, Construction, Engineering, Infrastructure, Property or other related technical markets.

You may already be operating at State Manager level, or you may be a successful Team Leader or Manager who is ready to take the next step.

You will bring:
  • A strong background in specialist recruitment within the WA market
  • At least one to two years’ experience leading a small team
  • A proven personal billing track record
  • The ability to win work and build lasting client relationships
  • A genuine interest in developing people and growing a business
  • A leadership style aligned with our values of Honest Communication, Focus, Feedback and Care
Why Design & Build?

Design & Build has been operating for more than 20 years, with offices in Perth, Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane.

Our vision is to become Australia’s most trusted recruitment agency. We measure ourselves against a simple mission: doing right by our clients, candidates, colleagues and community.

You will also receive:
  • A 35-hour working week with flexibility around start and finish times
  • Two work-from-home days each week
  • A fully paid Christmas shutdown in addition to annual leave
  • An additional day of leave for every year of service, providing up to 30 days of annual leave after five years
  • An annual all-expenses-paid High Achievers trip
  • Structured leadership development and ongoing coaching
  • Free and unlimited access to Sonder’s 24/7 wellbeing and safety support
  • Enhanced parental and compassionate leave
  • Support from experienced national leaders across operations, finance, people and culture, learning and development, and marketing
This is a genuine opportunity to inherit a strong platform, lead an established team and build a substantial WA recruitment business.

If you are an experienced recruitment leader ready to take ownership of a state and shape its next stage of growth, we would like to hear from you.

Apply confidentially or contact Andrew McGregor for a direct conversation.

job.title: Procurement Specialist
job.description:
About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Procurement / Commercial professional to support with the procurement of major projects up to $1b.
 
This role sits within a dedicated bidding office and plays a key part in end-to-end tender preparation, package procurement, and commercial analysis across multiple concurrent bids.

You will work closely with construction, estimating, and commercial teams to ensure trade packages are competitively procured, commercially sound, and aligned with program and delivery objectives.


Key Responsibilities
  • Manage hands-on procurement across up to 20 trade packages
  • Issue tender packages to market and coordinate supplier engagement
  • Liaise with construction and delivery teams to arrange supplier meetings and clarifications
  • Conduct commercial analysis including cost comparisons, valuations, and bid assessments
  • Review and interpret conditions of offer, inclusions/exclusions, and scope alignment
  • Support bid strategy development including options analysis and risk evaluation
  • Assess productivity impacts and program implications of subcontractor selections
  • Track and manage tender schedules, submissions, and procurement timelines
  • Deliver cost analysis and benchmarking to ensure best value outcomes
  • Contribute to end-to-end bid submissions (targeted for end of July)
  • Maintain strong awareness of market conditions and local trade capabilities
  • Ensure alignment with project sensitivities, including preference for local subcontractors where required
  • Support external valuation and commercial reporting requirements

Key Projects
  • Packages include numerous major projects including Defence, Sport Stadiums, Infrastructure, on JV delivery models

Working Environment
  • Based in a Melbourne CBD bidding office
  • Fast-paced tender environment with multiple concurrent bids

About You
  • Strong background in construction procurement or commercial management
  • Experience handling multiple trade packages simultaneously
  • Confident in cost analysis, commercial evaluation, and bid preparation
  • Strong numerical and analytical capability
  • Understanding of construction programs, productivity, and sequencing impacts
  • Ability to manage complex supplier and subcontractor negotiations
  • Strong market awareness and supplier network knowledge
  • Comfortable working in a high-pressure, deadline-driven bidding environment

Process
  • Initial contract engagement with potential for a permanent role
  • Interview process led in person at the Melbourne CBD office
  • Quick turnaround recruitment process

job.title: A07 Health & Wellbeing Advisor
job.description:
Public Sector People are partnering with the QLD State Government Department who are seeking an experienced Health and Wellbeing Principal Advisor (AO7) to lead and continuously improve enterprise-wide programs that protect worker health and support a safe, healthy and productive workforce.
  
Overview:
  • ASAP Start | Health and Wellbeing Principal Advisor (A07)
  • Attractive hourly rate from $87 per hour + 12% super
  • Initial contract until 31st March 2027 with potential for extension
  • QLD State Government
  • Brisbane CBD
  
Summary:

This specialist role leads worker health, wellbeing, fitness for work and hazardous exposure initiatives across a large Queensland civil construction workforce. Leveraging technical expertise, stakeholder engagement and organisational influence, the position drives enterprise-wide health outcomes, solves complex workforce challenges and delivers practical business-wide solutions without direct people management responsibilities.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead worker health programs including health monitoring, surveillance, contractor management and governance to ensure compliance and effective workforce health outcomes.
  • Oversee fitness for work and wellbeing initiatives, covering fatigue management, drug and alcohol programs, psychosocial risk management and employee wellbeing.
  • Manage hazardous exposure risks including silica, asbestos, lead, noise and chemicals through exposure monitoring, training and assurance activities.
  • Provide specialist advice and drive continuous improvement by developing policies, standards and practical organisation-wide solutions to health and wellbeing challenges.
What we are looking for:

The successful candidate will have access to occupational hygiene and specialist technical support when required; however, they will be expected to provide leadership, governance and program management across these disciplines and help continue maturing its approach to worker health and wellbeing.
  • Available ASAP, more than five years' experience in health, occupational hygiene, workplace wellbeing, health and safety or a closely related field.
  • Experience within construction, civil construction, transport, infrastructure, utilities, resources, rail or other comparable high-risk industries.
  • Strong experience implementing and managing fit-for-work programs, including fatigue and drug and alcohol management, leading psychosocial risk management programs and workplace wellbeing initiatives.
  • Experience developing enterprise-level frameworks, systems, standards, procedures and improvement programs, managing health risks associated with hazardous substances and hazardous exposures.

**This is a highly competitive role, and the hiring manager will be moving fast**
  
As an approved Government recruitment partner Public Sector People are ideally placed to assist you in your search for your next temporary or permanent opportunity.   
   
Best of luck!

job.description:
Finance Manager | Sydney | Full-time | Commercial Construction 

We are working with a growing Sydney-based construction business delivering a diverse portfolio of  commercial, heritage and infrastructure projects across NSW.

They are looking to appoint an experienced Finance Manager to take ownership of the day-to-day finance function and work closely with the Directors and broader project team.

The Role:

Reporting directly to the Directors, you will be responsible for overseeing the company's financial operations and providing commercial insight to support ongoing growth.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing the day-to-day finance function, including AP, AR, payroll and month-end processes
  • Preparing monthly management accounts, financial reporting and cash-flow forecasts
  • Managing WIP, project financials, revenue recognition and cost reporting
  • Monitoring project profitability, budgets, variations and financial performance
  • Supporting project teams with financial analysis and commercial reporting
  • Managing debtor and creditor relationships and ensuring effective cash-flow management
  • Preparing budgets, forecasts and financial models
  • Overseeing statutory compliance, BAS, GST, payroll tax and other financial obligations
  • Working closely with external accountants, auditors and other professional advisers
  • Reviewing and improving financial processes, systems and controls
  • Providing commercial advice and financial insights to the Directors
  • Supporting the business through continued growth and expansion
We are looking for an experienced Finance Manager / Senior Accountant who has a strong understanding of the construction industry and is comfortable taking ownership of a finance function.

You will ideally have:
  • Previous experience within construction, building, engineering or a related project-based environment
  • Strong understanding of project accounting, WIP, job costing and project profitability
  • Experience managing the full accounting function
  • Strong month-end, management reporting and forecasting skills
  • Excellent attention to detail and commercial acumen
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work closely with Directors and operational teams
  • Experience with Jobpac 
  • CA/CPA qualification or working towards qualification would be advantageous
