job.title: Unit Manager Parks Development
job.description:
About The City of Whittlesea

The City of Whittlesea is one of Australia’s fastest growing municipalities, supporting a diverse community of more than 220,000 people across established suburbs, growth areas and rural communities.
  
With continued growth comes significant investment in the parks, open spaces, sporting facilities and public realm that support connected and liveable communities.
  
This role presents an opportunity to lead the delivery of a diverse portfolio of highly visible projects that will help shape places used by the community every day.
  
About the Role
  
Reporting to the Manager Capital Delivery, the Unit Manager Parks Development is a senior leadership role responsible for the planning, design and delivery of Council’s parks, open space, sporting and public realm capital program.
  
Leading a team of experienced landscape architects and project managers, you will oversee a diverse portfolio spanning major park redevelopments, playgrounds, sports fields, streetscapes, town centres and broader open space improvements. The breadth of the program provides genuine variety, from smaller community-focused initiatives through to complex, high-profile capital works.
  
A key focus will be bringing a strong delivery and project management lens to the function. You will strengthen project governance, contract management and delivery disciplines while maintaining the design quality, creativity and landscape expertise already established within the team.
  
The role will oversee projects from design and procurement through construction and commissioning, while also directly managing selected priority projects. Acting as Superintendent across major contracts, you will work closely with contractors, consultants, government agencies, sporting clubs, community groups and internal stakeholders to deliver quality outcomes on time and within budget.
Just as importantly, this is a people leadership role. You will lead a capable and technically strong team, building on their expertise while creating greater collaboration, accountability and connection across the broader Capital Delivery department.

About You
  
You are an experienced capital delivery professional with a strong background across parks, open space, sporting, public realm or similarly complex community infrastructure.
  
Strong project and contract management capability will be important, with experience taking projects from initial planning and design through procurement, construction and completion.
  
You will understand the governance and commercial requirements of capital delivery and be comfortable managing contracts, budgets, risk and competing stakeholder priorities.
  
People leadership will be equally important. This is an intelligent, creative and technically capable team, and the role will suit someone who can provide clear direction, develop capability and encourage ideas, while bringing a strong focus on delivery and accountability.
  
A collaborative approach will be key. You will be comfortable building relationships across Council and working with government agencies, contractors, consultants and community stakeholders to navigate competing priorities and achieve practical outcomes.
  
A relevant tertiary qualification in Landscape Architecture or a similar discipline is required, together with substantial experience delivering capital infrastructure through major contracts.
  
Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with the City of Whittlesea to recruit this newly created opportunity within the Capital Delivery department.
  
For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.
  
To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.
  
Applications close Monday 5th October 2026.

job.title: HR & Industrial Relations Professionals | Multiple FIFO Opportunities
job.description:
HR & Industrial Relations Professionals | Multiple FIFO Opportunities
Officer | Advisor | Senior Advisor

Ready to take your HR or Industrial Relations career to the next level?

We're partnering with a leading organisation delivering one of Australia's most iconic and complex infrastructure projects and are seeking multiple HR and Industrial Relations professionals across Officer, Advisor and Senior Advisor level.

These FIFO positions offer the rare opportunity to work on a nationally significant project, partnering closely with operational leaders and a diverse workforce while gaining exposure to complex people, employee relations and industrial relations matters in a fast-paced construction environment.
Whether your expertise is in Human Resources, Industrial Relations or a combination of both, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Roles Working within an experienced People & Culture team, you'll provide practical HR and / OR IR support across a major project. Depending on your experience, your responsibilities may include:
  • Providing HR and/or IR advice to managers and employees across a large blue and white-collar workforce.
  • Interpreting and applying employment legislation, Awards and Enterprise Agreements.
  • Supporting employee relations matters including performance management, misconduct, disciplinary processes and workplace investigations.
  • Managing industrial relations matters, workplace compliance and stakeholder engagement.
  • Preparing employment contracts, correspondence and HR documentation.
  • Supporting workforce mobilisation, onboarding and HR administration activities.
  • Partnering with leaders to deliver practical people solutions and coaching.
  • Assisting with HR initiatives, culture programs and continuous improvement projects.
  • Delivering HR and IR training to leaders and employees.
  • Building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders to support successful project outcomes.
About You To be successful, you'll bring:
  • Experience in Human Resources, Industrial Relations or Employee Relations.
  • Sound knowledge of Australian employment legislation, including the Fair Work Act.
  • Experience interpreting Awards and Enterprise Agreements (highly regarded).
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • A proactive, collaborative and solutions-focused approach.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Human Resources, Employment Relations, Business, Law or a related discipline will be highly regarded.
Experience within construction, infrastructure, mining, engineering or other project-based environments will be highly regarded but is not essential.
What's on Offer
  • FIFO roster with accommodation, meals and travel provided.
  • The opportunity to contribute to one of Australia's landmark infrastructure projects.
  • Multiple opportunities available across Officer, Advisor and Senior Advisor level.
  • Exposure to complex HR and Industrial Relations matters within a large-scale project environment.
  • Work alongside experienced HR and IR professionals in a collaborative and supportive team.
  • Excellent career development and progression opportunities.
  • Competitive salary packages aligned with experience.
If you're looking for a career-defining opportunity where you can make a genuine impact on a nationally significant project, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now or contact Renee Hamilton at Design & Build Recruitment for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Coordinator Fleet and Urban Maintenance
job.description:
About Baw Baw Shire Council

Baw Baw Shire Council is a growing municipality located on the doorstep of metropolitan Melbourne, encompassing thriving townships, rural communities and some of Gippsland’s most attractive natural landscapes.
  
With continued growth placing increasing demand on Council services and infrastructure, Baw Baw is focused on building the capability, systems and services required to support its communities into the future.
  
This creates an exciting opportunity for an experienced operational leader to join the Open Space & Maintenance team and play an important role in how Council’s fleet and urban maintenance services continue to evolve.
  
About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Open Space & Maintenance, you will provide leadership across Council’s Fleet, Workshop and Urban Maintenance functions, with responsibility for a diverse in-house workforce of approximately 20 employees.
  
You will oversee services spanning Council’s fleet and plant, workshop operations, drainage and footpath maintenance, signage, street sweeping and public amenity cleansing.
  
A key focus of the role will be people leadership. You will support and develop your supervisors, create clarity around expectations and priorities, and continue building a collaborative and accountable culture across the depot.
  
Alongside the operational leadership, you will bring a strategic lense to how these services are planned and managed. This includes strengthening governance, systems and performance reporting, managing risk and compliance, and identifying opportunities to improve service delivery as the municipality continues to grow.
  
Fleet will form an important part of the portfolio, with Council managing approximately 450 vehicles and plant across operational, pool, commuter and private-use arrangements. You will oversee long-term fleet and replacement planning, workshop capability, lifecycle management and investment decisions to ensure Council’s fleet remains safe, compliant and financially sustainable.
  
The role will also provide strategic oversight across urban maintenance, ensuring appropriate service standards, maintenance programs and systems are in place across drainage, footpaths, signage, street sweeping and cleansing.
  
About You

We are looking for an experienced operational leader who combines strong people leadership with the ability to take a broader view of service delivery, risk and continuous improvement.
  
Experience leading operational services within a complex environment will be important, with exposure to fleet, asset management or municipal maintenance highly regarded. This is less about being a technical specialist across every area and more about bringing strong leadership and a broader strategic perspective.
  
Strong people leadership will be central to success. An approachable, practical and collaborative style, combined with experience developing supervisors and operational teams, managing performance and creating clear accountability, will be highly valued.
  
A sound understanding of fleet or asset lifecycle management, operational governance, safety and risk will be important, along with the commercial awareness to manage budgets, procurement and external service providers. Experience with heavy vehicle or Chain of Responsibility requirements will be advantageous, or alternatively the ability to quickly develop this knowledge.
  
Strong communication and stakeholder skills will complement the ability to balance day-to-day operational priorities with longer-term planning and continuous improvement.
  
Relevant tertiary qualifications in asset management, business, engineering, leadership, governance, project management or a related discipline, combined with substantial relevant experience, will be required.
  
Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Baw Baw Shire Council to recruit this opportunity on behalf of the Open Space & Maintenance team.
  
For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.
  
To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.
  
Applications close Tuesday 6th October at 5pm.

job.description:
$123,912–$142,499 + 12% super | Leaseback vehicle | Nine-day fortnight option | Hybrid working

Take the next step in your building surveying career with an experienced team, varied regulatory work and genuine support to develop your technical capability and registration.

Randwick City Council is seeking a registered Building Surveyor to join its Building Certification and Fire Safety team. This is a senior technical position offering broad exposure across building compliance, certification, fire safety and essential services within one of Sydney’s most diverse coastal communities.

You will work alongside experienced Building Surveyors and Essential Services Officers, assessing building matters, conducting inspections and helping property owners achieve safe and compliant outcomes.

Council is open to candidates at different stages of their building surveying careers. You may already have broad experience across a range of building types, or you may hold restricted registration and be looking for the support and exposure needed to continue developing.

The opportunity
Reporting within Council’s Compliance function, you will:
  • Assess and investigate complex building and fire-safety matters.
  • Support Council’s Essential Services and Fire Safety Program.
  • Review fire-safety schedules and Annual Fire Safety Statements.
  • Undertake inspections and assess compliance across Classes 2–9 buildings.
  • Recommend appropriate building and fire-safety upgrades.
  • Prepare and issue notices, orders, directions and regulatory correspondence.
  • Interpret and apply the NCC/BCA, NSW legislation and relevant Australian Standards.
  • Provide technical advice to colleagues, property owners and other stakeholders.
  • Help resolve sensitive compliance matters through clear communication and practical solutions.
  • Contribute to broader certification and regulatory work as Council continues to develop its capability.
The role has no direct reports but carries senior technical responsibility and provides the opportunity to support and guide other officers.

About you
You will be a registered Building Surveyor or Certifier with experience in building regulation, certification, compliance or fire safety.

You do not need to know the answer to every matter immediately. However, you must be able to identify the relevant legislation, codes and standards, undertake appropriate research and reach a clear, defensible decision.

Council is particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate:
  • Current registration as a Building Surveyor or Certifier in NSW.
  • Experience applying the NCC/BCA and relevant NSW legislation.
  • Exposure to Classes 2–9 buildings and complex fire-safety matters.
  • The ability to manage investigations, inspections and regulatory action.
  • Sound professional judgement and strong technical research skills.
  • Confidence handling difficult or sensitive customer matters.
  • A constructive approach to compliance focused on achieving safe outcomes.
  • A genuine interest in continuing to develop their registration and technical capability.
Experience in NSW local government would be advantageous, but candidates from private certification, consultancy and other relevant regulatory environments are encouraged to apply.

Why Randwick?
You will join an established and supportive team with significant experience across building certification, compliance and fire safety. Council is prepared to invest in the right person and support someone who wants to broaden their technical experience and progress their registration.

The position also offers:
  • Salary of $123,912–$142,499 + 12% super.
  • Leaseback vehicle.
  • Permanent full-time employment based on a 35-hour week.
  • The option to work a nine-day fortnight through Council’s flex arrangements.
  • Hybrid workplace arrangements available
  • Professional development and registration support.
  • Varied and technically challenging work across a prominent metropolitan LGA.
  • Access to Council wellbeing, mentoring, fitness and social initiatives.
  • An Eastern Suburbs location close to Sydney’s beaches and major transport connections.
If you are looking for a senior technical role where your judgement, communication and building-surveying expertise can make a visible contribution to community safety, we would welcome your application.

  • Stable, long-term role within a respected international organisation.

We are seeking an established practitioner with strong local government governance knowledge and experience advising elected representatives or comparable governing bodies. You will bring relevant expertise in executive recruitment, employment matters, performance assessment and contemporary remuneration practices, together with the confidence to facilitate challenging discussions and provide advice without fear or favour.

Your ability to build trust while maintaining independence will be central to your success. Previous experience chairing a CEO employment committee or undertaking comparable advisory work would be highly regarded, as would a demonstrated understanding of the relationship between Councillors and the organisation.

The commitment is expected to include mid-year and annual review meetings, quarterly reporting and additional advice and preparation as required. In-person attendance is expected at Council’s Rosebud, Mornington or Hastings offices.

job.title: Director Infrastructure Servces
job.description:
Director - Infrastructure Services
Build trust. Grow people. Deliver infrastructure that lasts.
The Hawkesbury is unlike anywhere else in metropolitan Sydney - and this is an opportunity to lead work that residents can see, use and value for generations.

Across approximately 2,776 square kilometres, Hawkesbury City Council is the custodian of an infrastructure asset portfolio valued at approximately $1.69 billion. Its road network includes 799 kilometres of sealed roads and 278 kilometres of unsealed roads across townships and rural villages.

We are looking for a Director who understands that infrastructure leadership is about more than delivering projects. It is about earning trust, developing people, making good decisions and creating lasting community value.

The opportunity
Reporting to the General Manager, you will join Council's Senior Executive Team and lead approximately 170 employees across asset management, capital delivery, infrastructure operations, waste and resource recovery, plant and fleet, and emergency management.

You will oversee a capital works program of approximately $120 million, including major road, building and community infrastructure projects.

The challenge is significant: strengthen asset management maturity, deliver an ambitious program, improve infrastructure resilience and transition from considerable grant-funded investment to a sustainable long-term program.

This is not a role for someone arriving with a fixed 'been there, done that' mindset. We want a leader who remains curious, develops themselves and others, challenges established thinking constructively and relentlessly pursues better community value.

What you will lead
  • Deliver major projects while strengthening cost, contract and program discipline.
  • Improve asset planning, data, prioritisation and lifecycle management.
  • Build resilient and sustainable infrastructure.
  • Develop managers, grow internal capability and create long-term succession.
  • Lead professional, operational and field-based teams with clarity and respect.
  • Build credibility with Councillors, employees, government partners and a highly engaged community.
  • Turn Council's values - Healthy, Efficient, Accountable, Respectful and Team Focused - into visible leadership behaviours.
What you will bring You may already be an experienced Director, or you may be an exceptional senior Manager or Executive Manager ready to step up. Your background could be in local or state government, an infrastructure owner, utility, consultancy or another complex asset-intensive organisation.

Essentially, you will bring:
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in engineering, construction, project management or a related discipline.
  • Extensive senior leadership experience in a complex statutory or regulated environment.
  • Strategic judgement and the confidence to operate in a political and community-facing setting.
  • Strong budgeting, cost-control, performance, project and contract-management capability.
  • Experience leading change, continuous improvement and a large multidisciplinary workforce.
  • Strong governance, probity, communication and stakeholder-management skills.
  • A genuine commitment to safety, wellbeing, inclusion and respectful leadership.
  • The resilience and adaptability to lead through competing priorities and changing circumstances.
  • Local government executive and emergency-management experience would be advantageous but is not essential.
The offer
The total remuneration package is $305,000-$315,000. The position is based at Council Chambers Administration Building in Windsor. Following the six-month probation period, Council's hybrid arrangement requires three days in the office and allows up to two days working from home.

Council is an equal opportunity employer. Hawkesbury City Council values a diverse and inclusive workplace representing the community we serve.
Public Sector People is committed to an accessible recruitment process. If you require support to participate in the process, please contact Alex Scott.

Start a confidential conversation If you want to lead visible, meaningful work and leave the Hawkesbury stronger for the future, we would welcome a conversation. To apply, submit your resume and a concise cover letter outlining your motivation and relevant experience.

job.title: Estimating Manager
job.description:
About the Company
A well-established residential building business based in Hamilton, Brisbane, is looking for an experienced Estimating Manager to take ownership of its estimating program.

Estimating sits at the centre of the business, with projects priced from in-house designs, quantity take-offs, supplier and trade rates. The business operates through a fully integrated Databuild and Onsite Companion workflow system.

With the current Estimating Manager moving on, this is an opportunity for an experienced estimator to step into a key position, take ownership of the estimating function and build on the systems already in place.

About the Role
As the Estimating Manager, you will take ownership of the estimating program while remaining hands-on with the day-to-day estimating function.
You will prepare take-offs, budgets and estimates, manage supplier and trade pricing, identify cost-saving opportunities and lead and mentor the estimating team.

Reporting directly to the Managing Director, you will work closely with the construction, operations and product development teams to ensure projects are accurately priced, cost-effective and aligned with the company's objectives.
This is a key role for someone who is committed, reliable and enthusiastic, with a strong focus on accuracy, efficiency, profitability and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities
  • Operate and maintain the integrated Databuild system, including cost codes, catalogues and pricing databases.
  • Maintain the flow of data between Databuild and Onsite Companion.
  • Prepare and review accurate quantity take-offs, bills of quantities and Job Analysis Reports.
  • Conduct technical plan reviews at both Preliminary Plans and Working Drawings stages.
  • Prepare detailed cost estimates for customer proposals, factoring in general and special conditions.
  • Ensure sales estimates meet required budgets and deadlines.
  • Develop scopes of works for external stakeholders.
  • Review supplier and subcontractor quotations and negotiate pricing to identify cost-saving opportunities.
  • Prepare project budgets for management approval and monitor actual costs against budget.
  • Report on project progress, costs and profitability to management.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Ensure subcontractor licences and insurances are current and accurately recorded in Onsite Companion.
  • Lead, mentor and support the estimating team.
  • Assist with internal projects and business initiatives as required.
About You To be successful in this role, you will have:
  • 5+ years' experience in construction estimating, ideally within residential building.
  • Strong, hands-on experience with Databuild, including operation, administration and maintaining pricing databases and cost codes.
  • Strong knowledge of cost estimation, bills of quantities and material take-offs.
  • Experience conducting technical plan reviews at Preliminary Plans and Working Drawings stages.
  • Experience preparing detailed budgets and analysing supplier and subcontractor quotations.
  • Strong understanding of subcontractor compliance, including licensing and insurance requirements.
  • Excellent negotiation and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • A highly analytical, organised and detail-oriented approach.
  • The ability to identify cost savings without compromising quality.
  • A proactive and results-driven approach, with a focus on process improvement.
  • The ability to manage multiple projects and changing priorities.
  • Relevant qualifications in construction management, quantity surveying or estimating, or equivalent industry experience.
Our Systems Hands-on Databuild experience is essential. The successful candidate will be trained on the other systems where required.
  • Databuild – Construction estimating, job costing and accounting.
  • Onsite Companion – Site and project management, linked with Databuild.
  • Therefore – Document management and invoice approval workflow.
The Opportunity This is an opportunity to step into a key position within a growing residential building business and have genuine ownership over the estimating function.

You will have the opportunity to lead an established estimating team, work directly with the Managing Director and contribute to improving systems, processes and profitability across the business.

If you are an experienced residential estimator with strong Databuild experience and are ready to take the next step into an Estimating Manager position, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now with your CV, or contact us for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Coordinator Infrastructure Planning and Development
job.description:
About Melton City Council

Melton City Council is one of Australia’s fastest-growing municipalities, located in Melbourne’s thriving western growth corridor. With significant population growth and infrastructure investment underway, Council is focused on ensuring the right infrastructure is planned and delivered at the right time to support its rapidly growing communities.
  
This growth creates an exciting opportunity for an experienced infrastructure planning professional to play a key leadership role in shaping Melton’s long-term infrastructure priorities and future investment.
  
About the Role

Reporting to the Manager City Infrastructure Planning, you will lead a multidisciplinary team responsible for shaping Melton’s long-term infrastructure planning and development.
  
A key focus will be coordinating and continually improving Council’s long-term capital works pipeline, bringing together growth forecasts, infrastructure priorities, financial considerations and project readiness to support confident investment decisions.
  
Working across Council, you will take a strategic view of future infrastructure needs, ensuring projects are appropriately planned, prioritised and aligned with Council’s broader financial and asset planning. You will work closely with capital works, community, open space, recreation and transport[AJ1]  planning, development contributions and other internal teams to understand the bigger picture and help determine what infrastructure is required, when it is needed and how it can be delivered.
  
The role also has significant external influence, building relationships and negotiating with State Government, developers, statutory authorities and service agencies around major roads, rail, schools, community infrastructure, utilities and other infrastructure required to support population growth.
  
You will also oversee strategic land acquisition activities and contribute to the ongoing improvement of infrastructure planning, governance and decision-making across Council.
  
In return, Melton City Council offers a genuinely flexible and supportive working environment, including:
  • 5 weeks annual leave
    • 13 ADOs per annum
    • Genuine flexible work options and hybrid working arrangements
    • Extensive Career Development & Leadership Programs
    • Access to the Local Government Employee Health Plan (GMHBA) with exclusive benefits
    • 16 weeks Paid Parental Leave (superannuation paid during parental leave)
    • 3 weeks Paid Secondary Carer Leave
    • Wellbeing initiatives
  
About You

You are an experienced infrastructure planning professional who combines strong strategic thinking with the people and stakeholder skills required to operate across a complex growth environment.
  
You will bring a strong understanding of infrastructure planning, ideally gained within local government, consulting, State Government or a comparable environment. Experience across growth area planning, capital works planning, asset management, development contributions or strategic infrastructure investment will be highly regarded.
  
An understanding of Council budgeting and the relationship between capital works, long-term financial planning and asset management will enable you to confidently assess priorities and support long-term investment decisions.
  
Importantly, this role requires a strong people leader. You will be collaborative and approachable, with the ability to develop a capable team, manage performance and create clarity around priorities and expectations.
  
Strong communication and influencing skills will be essential, along with the ability to simplify complex information, build trusted relationships and bring different stakeholders together around long-term infrastructure outcomes.
  
Tertiary qualifications in engineering, project management, strategy, business management or a related discipline will be highly regarded.
  
Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Melton City Council to recruit this opportunity on behalf of the City Infrastructure Planning team.
  
For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.
  
To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.
  
Applications close Monday 28th September 2026.

A well-established, Tier 2 construction and remedial contractor is experiencing strong, consistent growth across Sydney. The business specialises in remedial works, waterproofing, façade upgrades, concrete repair, and asset-protection projects across Class 2 buildings, aged care, high-rise residential, and live operational environments. With around 40 staff and a supportive, down-to-earth culture, the company is known for work-life balance, professional integrity, and long-term client relationships.

Due to newly awarded projects, the company is seeking an experienced Site Supervisor from the remedial space to take a lead role on site. 

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead day-to-day site operations and ensure smooth delivery across seven rooftop zones.
  • Coordinate, manage, and mentor subcontractors, trades, and site teams.
  • Ensure the site operates safely at all times, especially regarding working at heights in a live environment.
  • Interpret design drawings, implement remedial solutions, and work closely with engineers and consultants.
  • Oversee site logistics, scheduling, sequencing, and daily workflows.
  • Drive high-quality workmanship across all remedial, waterproofing, and reinstatement activities.
  • Conduct site inspections, identify risks, resolve issues, and escalate where necessary.
  • Maintain thorough site documentation: daily logs, inductions, SWMS, safety checks, and progress tracking.
  • Work closely with the Project Manager to align site progress with program, budget, and design intent.
  • Build strong relationships with clients, residents, consultants, and internal stakeholders.
About You / Requirements
  • Proven experience as a Site Supervisor within construction (remedial experience is required).
  • Strong understanding of construction methodologies, sequencing, and technical detail.
  • Ability to interpret drawings, remedial scopes, and technical design requirements.
  • Excellent leadership skills with the ability to motivate and direct on-site teams.
  • Strong organisation and planning capability, able to manage multiple work fronts at once.
  • High attention to detail with a quality-driven mindset.
  • Confident communicator who can liaise effectively with residents, subcontractors, and consultants.
  • Safety-focused, with valid construction certifications and ideally heights-related tickets.

What’s On Offer / Salary Package
  • Salary: $140k-$160k + Super + Company Car / Car Allowance 
  • Monday - Friday work week (No Saturdays - legitimately)
  • Long-term project stability 
  • Family-based culture where everyone is known by name; no corporate layers.
  • Social events every 12 weeks 
  • Paid for overtime
  • Down-to-earth management team who value work-life balance.
  • Growth opportunities within a rapidly expanding business.
For any questions relating to this role or other opportunities with Design & Build and our clients please contact Emily Collins on 0468927246 or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential.

job.title: Lead Power Systems Engineer
job.description:
Position: Lead Power Systems Engineer
Location: Adelaide, SA
Salary: Up to $185,000 base + super

Design & Build is working with an established Australian EPC contractor growing its engineering team across major transmission, substation and renewable energy projects.

We’re looking for a Lead Power Systems Engineer with strong hands-on modelling and analysis experience who can make an immediate technical impact within the team.

Why Join?
  • Strong pipeline of transmission and substation projects
  • Work within an established multidisciplinary engineering team
  • Exposure from studies and detailed design through to construction

The Role

This is broader than a traditional grid connection role. You’ll take ownership of the power systems studies and modelling required to support HV substation design, working closely with primary, secondary and protection engineers throughout detailed design and delivery.

What You'll Do
  • Independently perform power systems studies and detailed modelling
  • Deliver network analysis required for HV substation design
  • Perform load flow, short circuit and network stability analysis
  • Develop and validate models for transformers, transmission lines, generators and inverter-based resources
  • Assess designs against NER, AEMO and NSP requirements
  • Interpret study results and provide practical recommendations to the design team
  • Support projects through detailed design and commissioning
  • Review technical work and mentor junior engineers
What We're Looking For
  • 5+ years’ experience in power systems engineering
  • Strong hands-on modelling and analysis capability
  • Experience delivering studies in support of HV substation design
  • Strong DIgSILENT PowerFactory experience
  • PSCAD experience highly regarded
  • Australian transmission, substation or NSP project experience
  • Strong understanding of Australian network standards and requirements
Apply now or contact Jasmine Wiklander on 0405 437 667 for a confidential discussion.

All applications will be treated with strict confidentiality.

job.title: AO6 Senior Financial Accountant
job.description:
Public Sector People is partnering with a Queensland State Government Department to source an experienced AO6 Senior Financial Accountant for their Finance team. This is a contract role running through to 31 January 2027, based in Brisbane CBD.

About the Team

The Corporate Finance team supports the Chief Finance Officer in leading the department's financial accounting processes and policies. The team plays a key role in the preparation of the department's financial statements and in developing operational policies, procedures and practices that support sound financial management.

Your Role
Reporting into Corporate Finance, you'll bring strong technical financial accounting expertise to support internal controls, compliance and audit activity, while contributing to the department's month-end, EOFY and financial reporting obligations.

Your Responsibilities
  • Monitor key internal controls, finance systems and assurance activities to validate financial compliance
  • Develop and implement internal controls, proactively identifying risk
  • Provide expert advice on the resolution of internal and external audit issues
  • Apply expert knowledge to the design and implementation of financial processes and procedures, including maintenance of the department's Financial Management and Practice Manual (FMPM) and financial delegations
  • Contribute to the CFO Assurance Plan and related activities supporting the CFO assurance statement
  • Provide financial management advice and support to departmental staff
  • Contribute to end-of-month and end-of-financial-year activities, including journal review and preparation
  • Conduct financial reconciliations, ensuring integrity of the department's general ledgers
  • Support the identification of training needs in financial accounting and contribute to training program development
  • Maintain the integrity of the department's financial accounting records and systems in line with accounting standards, legislative and departmental requirements
  • Assist with financial system upgrades, enhancements and testing
What We're Looking For
  • Demonstrated experience in a similar Senior Financial Accountant role, ideally within Queensland State Government or the broader public sector

job.title: Head of Parks and Urban Forest
job.description:
HEAD OF PARKS AND URBAN FOREST
  
About Moonee Valley City Council

Moonee Valley City Council is a diverse and vibrant municipality in Melbourne’s inner north-west, delivering a broad range of services that support the amenity, environment and everyday experience of the community.
  
Council is focused on delivering high-quality, responsive and sustainable services while continuing to strengthen how its operations are planned, managed and delivered.
  
This position presents an exciting opportunity to lead one of Council’s largest operational functions and shape the future delivery of its parks, open space and urban forest services.
  
About the Role
  
The Head of Parks and Urban Forest is a senior position responsible for the planning and delivery of Council’s sports fields, conservation, parks, cityscapes and tree services, ensuring high standards of presentation, amenity, safety and environmental performance.
  
Reporting to the Manager City Presentation, you will oversee a large multidisciplinary operational function, with responsibility for developing capability, strengthening performance and creating a positive and accountable team culture. With much of the service delivered in-house, a key priority will be strengthening workforce planning, scheduling and resource allocation to support efficient and responsive service delivery.
  
The role will take a broader view of how the function operates, identifying opportunities to improve systems, processes and service performance while building capability and accountability across the team. You will also oversee budgets and key contracts, balancing operational priorities with safety, service quality and value for the community.
  
Working collaboratively across Council and with community stakeholders, you will help ensure these highly visible services continue to respond to organisational priorities, environmental outcomes and community expectations.
  
About You
  
You are an experienced operational leader with a background across parks, trees, open space, sports grounds or a related service environment. Experience at Coordinator level or above within Local Government, or in a similarly complex service delivery environment, will be highly regarded.
  
Importantly, you will bring strong people management capability, with experience overseeing sizeable and diverse operational teams. You know how to build capability, set clear expectations and create a culture of accountability, safety and high performance, while confidently managing change and addressing performance when required.
  
You bring the ability to step beyond day-to-day operational requirements and look at the bigger picture, identifying opportunities to improve workforce planning, resource allocation, scheduling and the way services are delivered.
  
Commercial and financial capability will also be important, with experience managing budgets, contractors and resources and making considered decisions around service quality, cost and value.
  
A collaborative and pragmatic approach will be key. You will be comfortable building strong relationships across Council, engaging with the community and bringing people with you as the function continues to evolve.
  
A relevant tertiary qualification directly related to the portfolio is required, with postgraduate qualifications in business management or a related discipline viewed favourably.
  
Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Moonee Valley City Council to recruit this newly created opportunity within the City Presentation department.
  
For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.
  
To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.
Applications close at 5pm Tuesday 29th September 2026.

job.title: Safety Advisor
job.description:
I’m currently representing a well-established developer builder looking to appoint an experienced Safety Advisor for a major high-rise residential development on the Gold Coast.

The project is in its early stages, giving you the opportunity to have a genuine impact on the safety culture and systems from the ground up.

The Role
  • Support the day-to-day HSE function across the project.
  • Conduct site inspections, audits, observations and risk assessments.
  • Review SWMS, permits and high-risk construction activities.
  • Monitor crane operations, lifting, working at heights and other critical activities.
  • Support incident investigations, corrective actions and safety reporting.
  • Deliver inductions, toolbox talks and safety briefings.
  • Engage with subcontractors and site teams to drive a proactive safety culture.
  • Ensure compliance with WHS legislation, company and project requirements.
About You
  • 3–5+ years’ experience in a Safety/HSE role within Australian construction.
  • Previous high-rise, commercial or residential construction experience.
  • Strong understanding of WHS legislation, risk management and contractor engagement.
  • Confident communicating with site teams, subcontractors and senior management.
  • Practical, proactive and solutions-focused approach to safety.
  • Relevant WHS qualifications.
What's On Offer
  • Join during the early stages of construction.
  • Competitive salary – up to $200K package
  • Exposure to a dual-tower project with tower cranes and complex construction activities.
  • Established developer builder with a strong project pipeline.
  • Long-term opportunity and genuine career progression.
If you'd like to learn more about this role or explore other HSE opportunities across Brisbane and South East Queensland, contact Claire Ireland on 0412 951 013 or click Apply.

job.title: Site Manager
job.description:
The Company

An Australian owned construction business specialising in technically complex Defence, government and commercial projects. With a director-led approach, the business combines robust management systems with the agility and personal accountability of a hands-on project team.

Their work spans new build construction, building refurbishments, infrastructure upgrades and projects within live, sensitive environments. They have established a reputation for strong client relationships, quality delivery and the ability to manage complex works while maintaining operational continuity.

With projects across Sydney and regional NSW, they are seeking an experienced Site Manager who enjoys taking ownership of projects and is comfortable working away from home when required.

The Opportunity

Due to a growing pipeline of Defence and commercial projects, an opportunity exists for an experienced Site Manager to join the team. 

Projects may be located anywhere from Albury–Wodonga through to Newcastle, with opportunities also available across Sydney. The successful candidate must be comfortable with regional assignments and periods working away from home, with accommodation and applicable living away from home allowances provided.

This role will suit a capable Site Manager who thrives in a hands-on environment, enjoys the variety of different project locations and wants to work closely with experienced directors and project teams.

The Role

Reporting to the Project Manager, you will be responsible for:
  • Managing day-to-day site operations from commencement through to completion
  • Coordinating subcontractors, suppliers and site personnel across multiple work fronts
  • Driving construction programs, sequencing and key project milestones
  • Maintaining high standards of safety, quality and environmental compliance
  • Managing site logistics, deliveries and access requirements
  • Ensuring works are delivered in accordance with drawings, specifications and contractual requirements
  • Coordinating with consultants, clients and project stakeholders
  • Managing works within live or operational environments where required
  • Identifying and resolving site issues, risks and buildability challenges
  • Maintaining site records, reporting and quality documentation
  • Leading inspections, defect management and project handover
About You
  • Proven experience as a Site Manager within commercial, government or Defence construction
  • Defence project experience highly preferable, particularly within live or secure environments
  • Strong understanding of construction programming, subcontractor coordination and site management
  • Experience delivering new-build, refurbishment or technically complex construction projects
  • Excellent knowledge of WHS, quality assurance and compliance requirements
  • Strong communication and leadership skills with a proactive, solutions-focused approach
  • Comfortable working away from home on regional projects when required
  • Relevant trade or construction qualifications
  • Ability to obtain and maintain required Defence security clearances and site access, where applicable
In Return
  • Salary up to $200,000 + Super
  • Fully maintained vehicle
  • Accommodation provided for regional assignments
  • Tax-free Living Away From Home Allowance (LAFHA), where eligible
  • Fortnightly flights home Friday - Monday when working on projects away from home
  • Diverse project locations across Sydney and regional NSW
  • Exposure to technically interesting Defence and commercial projects
  • Work closely with experienced directors and a supportive project team
  • Genuine autonomy and the opportunity to take ownership of project delivery
  • Long-term career opportunities within a growing construction business
How to Apply Click Apply and include your CV and project list (Word format preferred).

For a confidential discussion about this opportunity, contact Mitchell Barker on 0423 927 536.

All applications will be treated with strict confidentiality.

job.title: Earthworks & Quarry Supervisor (Perth)
job.description:
About the Business:
Our client is a well established civil contracting business with more than two decades of continuous operation across the Perth metropolitan area. Widely regarded as a leader in ground level civil works, they have built a strong reputation through an unwavering commitment to safety, operational efficiency, and forward thinking delivery methods. Respected by peers and clients alike, this is an organisation that has earned its standing through consistent performance and not just reputation.

About the role:
Due to a strong forward project pipeline spanning multiple metropolitan corridors, we are currently seeking an experienced site supervisors to step into a pivotal leadership role. The position sits at the heart of active site delivery, placing you in command of crews, coordinating plant and equipment, and ensuring projects are delivered on time and to standard.

This is an organisation that genuinely invests in its people. Progression from within is the norm, not the exception, and work life balance is taken seriously and not just talked about.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Directing and coordinating site crews to hit project milestones
  • Overseeing the deployment and operation of heavy plant and equipment
  • Upholding site compliance across safety, quality, and procedural requirements
  • Planning and scheduling daily site activities to maximise productivity
  • Acting as the key liaison between site and project management, providing regular updates and resolving issues as they arise
  • Mentoring team members and actively building capability across your crew

To be successful in this role you will have:
  • A solid background in earthworks and civil construction site environments
  • Demonstrated experience supervising site teams and managing project delivery
  • Strong working knowledge of heavy machinery and plant operations
  • Proven leadership ability with a track record of bringing out the best in those around you

What's in it for you:
  • A varied and active project pipeline with genuine long term stability
  • A business culture built around internal development and real career progression
  • A genuine work life balance that is lived, not just listed on a job ad
  • Competitive remuneration between $120k - $150k + Superannuation with clear pathways for advancement, depending on experience.

job.title: Slab Starts Supervisor
job.description:
A well‑known Perth residential builder is looking for a switched‑on Site Start Supervisor to manage the setup phase of new home builds across both NOR and SOR.

If you’re organised, confident with early‑stage coordination, and enjoy getting jobs ready for slab down, this role will suit you perfectly.

You’ll take ownership of everything needed to get a site build‑ready — early trades, documentation checks, materials, surveys, and making sure each job kicks off smoothly.

Day‑to‑day includes:
  • Checking plans, engineering, energy reports and approvals
  • Organising surveys, earthworks, access, fencing and safety
  • Ordering early‑stage materials (plumbing, concrete, frames, hardware)
  • Booking and coordinating early trades
  • Fixing issues before they slow down the build
  • Handing over cleanly to the main Site Supervisor

What You’ll Bring
  • Residential construction experience (site, scheduling, pre‑start or coordination)
  • Trade background ideal — carpentry and brick laying ideal 
  • Great for someone stepping off the tools and wanting to grow into a supervisor role
  • Familiar with the residential building process and how jobs flow
  • Strong organisation and attention to detail
  • Confidence dealing with trades and suppliers
  • Ability to juggle multiple jobs across NOR & SOR with a team
  • A proactive, solutions‑focused mindset
What’s On Offer
  • Up to $115k + super + vehicle
  • A steady pipeline of work and long‑term stability
  • Supportive construction leadership and clear processes
  • A builder known for communication, quality and client care
Interested to learn more?
Apply now or reach out to Kiralee Barker for a confidential chat or to stay informed about upcoming 2026 opportunities. kiralee@designandbuild.com.au  | 0478 113 223

job.title: Reporting Lead
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced and commercially focused Reporting Lead to drive reporting, analytics, and automation capabilities across the organisation. This role will lead the design, development, automation, and optimisation of enterprise reporting solutions while partnering with senior business leaders to deliver actionable insights that support strategic decision-making.

The successful candidate will combine deep technical expertise in Power BI, SQL, Microsoft Fabric, and report automation with exceptional stakeholder management skills. You will be responsible for transforming complex business requirements into scalable reporting and analytics solutions that improve visibility, performance, and decision-making across the business.

This is an opportunity to lead the evolution of a modern reporting function, leveraging Microsoft's data and analytics platform to build enterprise-grade, automated reporting capabilities.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the organisation's reporting and analytics capability, ensuring reliable, scalable, and business-focused reporting solutions.
  • Design, develop, and maintain enterprise-grade dashboards, reports, and visualisations using Power BI.
  • Develop and optimise datasets, semantic models, and reporting architectures using SQL and modern data platform technologies.
  • Leverage Microsoft Fabric to support data integration, transformation, governance, analytics, and reporting initiatives.
  • Lead the automation of reporting processes to reduce manual effort, improve accuracy, and increase reporting timeliness.
  • Design and implement automated data pipelines, report refresh schedules, alerting mechanisms, and report distribution processes.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline reporting workflows and eliminate manual reporting activities across the organisation.
  • Partner with senior executives and business leaders to understand strategic objectives, reporting requirements, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Translate complex business requirements into technical reporting and analytics solutions.
Skills & Experience Essential
  • Extensive experience in a Reporting Lead, BI Lead, Analytics Lead, or similar senior reporting role.
  • Advanced expertise in Power BI, including:
    • Data modelling
    • DAX
    • Power Query
    • Dashboard and report development
    • Performance optimisation
  • Strong hands-on experience with SQL for data extraction, transformation, and analysis.
  • Proven experience working with and implementing solutions within Microsoft Fabric environments.
  • Demonstrated experience delivering report automation and enterprise reporting solutions.
  • Strong understanding of automated reporting processes, data orchestration, scheduling, and workflow optimisation.
  • Experience automating data ingestion, transformation, reporting, and dashboard refresh processes.
  • Exceptional senior stakeholder management skills, including the ability to engage, influence, and challenge executive stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to gather requirements, define reporting strategies, and translate business needs into technical solutions.
Desirable
  • Experience with Azure Data Platform technologies.
  • Knowledge of data governance, data quality, and reporting frameworks.
  • Experience leading reporting, analytics, or business intelligence teams.
  • Relevant Microsoft certifications in Power BI, Fabric, Data Analytics, or Azure.
  • Experience supporting self-service reporting and analytics initiatives.
What Success Looks Like
  • A trusted advisor to senior leadership on reporting, analytics, and data strategy.
  • Delivery of accurate, timely, and impactful business insights.
  • Significant reduction in manual reporting through automation and process improvement.
  • Increased adoption and maturity of Power BI and Microsoft Fabric capabilities.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and measurable business outcomes driven by data.
  • Improved reporting governance, efficiency, scalability, and data quality across the organisation.
Interested in exploring? Apply now! Interviews will be commencing soon.

job.title: A08 Operations Manager (Owners Representative)
job.description:
This QLD State Government department is seeking an experienced Operations Manager (Owner’s Representative) to provide operational leadership, governance and assurance for a first-of-its-kind critical minerals processing facility.

Acting as the Queensland Government’s on-site representative, you will play a key role in building strong relationships, aligning multiple stakeholders and creating a high-performing operational environment as the facility progresses through commissioning and into early operations.

This is a highly collaborative role requiring an experienced leader who can work effectively with operators, contractors, technical specialists, government stakeholders and customers. The ability to influence, communicate clearly and build trust across diverse groups will be critical to success.

Key Responsibilities
  • Act as the Owner’s Representative, building strong relationships and translating owner, contractor and customer requirements into clear operational expectations.
  • Provide visible operational leadership and establish a positive culture of accountability, collaboration and performance.
  • Establish and maintain the operational governance and assurance framework for early operations.
  • Build effective working relationships across operators, contractors, suppliers, advisors, government stakeholders and customers.
  • Drive performance through structured governance, reporting, communication and decision-making processes.
  • Influence outcomes across multiple organisations and stakeholder groups, including where there is no direct line authority.
  • Lead operational and campaign readiness reviews and provide recommendations for go/no-go decisions.
  • Foster strong operating discipline, performance routines and timely close-out of actions and commitments.
  • Provide on-site oversight of high-risk activities and ensure critical controls are effectively implemented.
  • Monitor operational performance and work collaboratively with stakeholders to identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities.
  • Chair performance, defect and improvement forums to drive accountability, collaboration and operational availability.
  • Provide high-quality advice, briefings and recommendations to senior stakeholders and government representatives.
  • Support commercial activities including contract development, procurement and broader stakeholder engagement.
  • Maintain robust Management of Change (MOC) processes and support sound asset management and reliability practices.
Successful Candidate
Leadership & People Management
  • Significant experience in operations leadership, operational management, Owner’s Representative or operational assurance roles within complex industrial, resources, minerals processing or similarly high-risk environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead, influence and engage people across multiple teams, organisations and professional disciplines.
  • Proven ability to establish a culture of accountability, collaboration, safety and high performance.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build trust and credibility with operators, contractors, technical specialists, senior executives and government stakeholders.
  • Experience managing competing priorities and bringing diverse stakeholders together to achieve common operational outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes without relying solely on direct line authority.
Operational & Industry Experience
  • Experience supporting commissioning, start-up or early operations of processing, resources, infrastructure or other complex industrial facilities.
  • Strong understanding of operational governance, risk management, Management of Change and operational assurance principles.
  • Experience in minerals, resources, processing or related heavy industry environments is highly desirable, but not essential for the right operational leader.
  • Practical experience verifying critical controls and making sound, risk-based operational decisions.
  • A strong understanding of operational performance, reliability and continuous improvement.
Stakeholder & Commercial Skills
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently with a broad range of stakeholders and prepare clear reports, advice and briefings for senior decision-makers.
  • Proven ability to develop and maintain productive relationships across multiple organisations and stakeholder groups.
  • Strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills, with the ability to resolve issues and maintain alignment in a complex environment.
  • Commercial acumen and experience with contract management, procurement and supplier relationships.
  • Strong project management and operational planning capability.
  • Ability to analyse information, identify opportunities and drive improvements in an evolving operational environment.
Qualifications & Requirements
  • Current open C Class Driver Licence.
  • Construction White Card.
  • Australian citizenship, permanent residency or valid work rights in Australia.
  • Willingness to travel as required.
  • Ability to successfully complete criminal history and conflict of interest checks.
This role offers a unique opportunity for an experienced operations and people leader to play a key role in establishing and governing operations for a strategically important critical minerals facility.

You will have the opportunity to work across government, industry and technical stakeholders while helping establish the culture, relationships and operating framework for a new facility that will contribute to Queensland’s growing advanced manufacturing, resources and critical minerals sector.

Send your resume through to daniel@publicsectorpeople.com.au and give me a call on 0466 265 446 today to discuss this role in further detail.
